belief: People in authority can't be trusted.
origins: If a parent, teacher, coach, pastor, or boss abused or betrayed authority, the lesson may stay: authority means danger. We may bristle at supervision, expect to be used, or avoid anyone who has power over us. Real experiences of misuse of power deserve to be taken seriously.
teaches: The Bible shows both sides. Paul writes, “Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God.” Yet when the council ordered the apostles to stop speaking, Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.” The psalmist says, “It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man.” And “The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.” Authority is not always safe, and it is not always unsafe. We can trust God ultimately, and trust people in proportion to their character.
self_statements: Anyone with power will misuse it.
They will use me and then drop me.
I cannot rely on bosses or leaders.
If I submit, I will be hurt.
I have to protect myself from them.
errors: Treating every authority as the one who hurt me.
Believing authorities are either totally safe or totally dangerous.
Feeling wary and concluding that all authority is dangerous.
questions: Who in authority hurt or betrayed me, and what happened?
Have any people in authority treated me fairly or kindly?
How can I tell a trustworthy leader from an unsafe one?
What does Scripture say about obeying God over people when they conflict?
How might distrust affect my work and relationships?
What would healthy, measured trust look like?
truth: Some people in authority have misused their power, and my caution makes sense. Not all are the same. I can trust God above all, and I can extend trust to people in proportion to their character, with wise boundaries.
hw_truths: My ultimate trust is in the Lord.
God directs hearts where He pleases.
I can obey God over people when they conflict.
log: Each week, note one interaction where you gave measured trust and what happened.
actions: Write what happened with the authority who hurt you.
Write signs of safe leadership, such as honesty, consistency, and humility.
Extend small trust to someone who shows these qualities.
Talk to a counselor if your experiences involved abuse.
prayer: Lord, some who held authority over me hurt me. Heal that wound. Teach me to trust You above all and to discern who is safe. Amen.
hw_questions: What signs show a safe leader?
When do I obey God over people?
What does measured trust look like?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I take refuge in the Lord first, and I can trust people carefully.”
